key_insight: 3D Cartesian PDE solvers can be reduced exactly to repeated 1D line operations via tensor-product/Kronecker structure, so the 3D operator is never assembled in memory.
engineering_relevance: This makes matrix-free CFD and PDE solvers faster, more memory-efficient, and easier to scale across CPUs/GPUs and MPI domains while preserving exact separability.
method: Use Kronecker-product algebra to rewrite 3D operators as separable 1D kernels along x, y, and z.
Apply multi-right-hand-side reshaping so each sweep becomes a batched line solve or stencil kernel.
Use sum factorization and pencil decomposition to reduce quadrature cost and maintain contiguous direction-wise communication.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports asymptotic outcomes rather than experiments: fixed stencil width or polynomial degree gives O(N) compute, O(Nx+Ny+Nz) storage up to bandwidth constants, and direct Poisson/Helmholtz methods add only the expected transform cost.
watch_item: Performance depends on implementation details such as bandwidth, cache locality, and MPI pencil layout; the asymptotic gains do not remove communication or transform overheads.
paper_title: No 3D Matrices: A Unified Tensor-Product View of Matrix-Free Cartesian PDE Solvers
